verdict: Caution: lend selectively to organised modular-furniture units with domestic order books; avoid export-dependent wood-carving and raw-material traders until demand recovers.
title: Saharanpur wooden & modular furniture: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Saharanpur runs on wood: carving units, handicraft exporters and, increasingly, modular-furniture assemblers who buy plywood, MDF and sawn timber, cut and finish it, and sell either to export buyers or to domestic dealers and projects. **Cash is made in the conversion step, not in the timber** — margin sits in design, finishing and delivery, and the organised players say the market is crowded with unorganised and big organised competitors alike [6]. Working capital is the real business: raw material is bought upfront, inventory sits as seasoning and work-in-progress, and export or project receivables stretch the cycle. Capex is modest for carving units but real for anyone adding MDF lines or panel processing. **So when a proposal lands, check the inventory-and-receivable days first; if the cycle is funded by suppliers rather than the borrower's own margin, ask what happens when a buyer delays.**

## What has changed now
Local reporting is blunt: demand for wood raw material has fallen, even sales of sandpaper and brushes are down, and thousands of families' livelihoods are affected [1]. Export demand is falling while costs rise, and artisans are bearing the brunt [2][3]. **This is a demand-side squeeze on the traditional carving/export cluster, not a cost shock alone.** The official data pack reads better than the street: the data-based call is OK at 79, with Uttar Pradesh GST collections up 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and all-India furniture-linked output (NIC 31) up 9.4% YoY [D]. **Treat the state GST number as a tailwind for domestic-facing units, not a rescue for exporters.** Note the local sources are from August–September 2026 and describe conditions then.

## Where the growth is
Peer results point the same way: Greenply's Q2FY27 plywood revenue rose 15.5% with realisation up 9% [7], and Dhabriya Polywood won a Rs 25.30 crore order from the Godrej Group through its modular-furniture subsidiary [4]. **Pursue organised modular-furniture makers with domestic institutional or builder order books, panel-processing units feeding them, and plywood/MDF dealers with clean GST and steady dealer networks.** Avoid pure export-carving units with falling order books [2][3] and raw-material traders whose volumes are already shrinking [1]. Where a borrower claims export recovery, collect from customer the buyer-wise order position and last twelve months' shipment values.

## How to grow safely
Structure term loans against installed machinery, not against land, and keep working-capital limits sized to a cycle you have verified. Ask for the top-five buyer concentration every quarter; if one buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for the contract and payment history.

## Early-warning signs
- **Monthly GST turnover falling two quarters running** -> freeze enhancement, review limit. - **Inventory days rising while sales fall** -> ask for ageing; if finished goods dominate, cut exposure. - **Cheque or LC delays from a single export buyer** -> seek diversion of proceeds, reduce limit. - **Power-cost or wage arrears** -> check statutory dues before any renewal.
